name: PUF Adaptive Auth for IoT
sub: IIT Guwahati IoT Lab · protocol design
short: Three-phase adaptive authentication protocol using Physically Unclonable Functions to secure IoT devices like remote EV charging stations.
full: A lightweight three-phase authentication protocol for resource-constrained IoT devices, built around Physically Unclonable Functions so device identity cannot be cloned and the PUF response is never transmitted directly. Pre-shared key exchange, enrollment, then authentication: the server issues a challenge and seed, the device returns a derived response, and the server verifies it. Default authentication skips encryption to stay fast; a threat score escalates to encrypted exchanges when replay or MITM activity is detected. Simulated end-to-end with a Python client (device/app) and server (control station), tested across legal-user, attacker, and high-threat scenarios.
